title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent
summary: TGR-EvoDAG replaces linear or general-purpose LLM-driven code evolution for generative recommendation pipelines with a DAG-based multi-agent framework that maintains parallel evolution branches, merges complementary innovations, and adds stage-aware cost planning plus active downstream co-adaptation across the tokenization, pre-training, and alignment stages. The cost is substantial orchestration complexity: running a multi-agent evolutionary search over full pipeline retraining requires repeated GPU-hour expenditure per candidate and a working GR pipeline with per-stage diagnostic evaluation infrastructure, which is realistic for a platform like Tencent but heavy for a small team. It can fail when the reader lacks a GR pipeline to evolve, when evaluation signals are noisy enough to misguide branch selection, or when the compute budget cannot sustain the evolutionary search the gains presuppose.
rationale: The method targets industrial-scale generative recommendation with evolutionary retraining budgets and platform-level online A/B validation, so a constrained-infrastructure team should track it rather than adopt it, though its stage-aware cost planning and downstream co-adaptation ideas are worth borrowing if the reader already operates a multi-stage GR pipeline.
technique: DAG-based multi-agent code evolution for generative recommendation

The cost is substantial orchestration complexity: running a multi-agent evolutionary search over full pipeline retraining requires repeated GPU-hour expenditure per candidate and a working GR pipeline with per-stage diagnostic evaluation infrastructure, which is realistic for a platform like Tencent but heavy for a small team. On public Amazon datasets, offline metrics improve by up to 37.4% and Agent4Rec simulated user satisfaction by 19.7% over the strongest baseline; industrial deployment on Tencent's platform shows 12.16% relative offline Hit@1 improvement and a statistically significant 0.40% online CTR increase.
